events: counter a spell or nonmana ability
state_writes: ordinary countered-spell movement to its owner's graveyard
timing: the bounded effect executes during resolution after target revalidation
targets: one current public spell, activated ability, or triggered ability in a closed target domain
a counter instruction cannot target its own stack object
choices: the acting player chooses one legal public stack target while announcing the spell or ability
hidden_information: the bounded family reads and projects only public stack and public destination information
apnap: ordinary multiplayer priority determines when a counter spell or ability may be announced
layers: only an exact trusted intrinsic 'This spell can't be countered' declaration is represented by this slice
replacement_effects: alternate destinations and replacement effects for countered spells remain outside this bounded slice
copy: spell copies are stack objects and ordinary copies do not inherit an intrinsic prohibition from the copied physical card unless the stack snapshot says so
control_change: the current stack controller supplies counter-prohibition and telemetry context
zone_change: a countered physical spell ordinarily moves from the stack to its owner's graveyard
a countered ability leaves the stack without moving a card
source_leaves: the resolving counter instruction does not require its physical source to remain in its prior zone

variants: mandatory direct counter target typed spell domain
mandatory direct counter target activated or triggered ability

implementation.component: closed direct-counter compiler, strict semantic handler, typed stack-counter owner, target revalidation, and trusted intrinsic prohibition declaration
implementation.supported_slice: Mandatory direct one-target counter clauses over the closed spell and nonmana-ability domains, plus the complete intrinsic sentence 'This spell can't be countered'.

known_blockers: conditional-payment, optional, modal, mass, multi-target, linked-result, and alternate-destination counter clauses remain residual
conditional, source-qualified, name-qualified, target-qualified, and variable-mana-value stack predicates remain residual
conditional, source-qualified, granted, and temporary counter prohibitions beyond existing typed cast context remain unsupported
complete counter replacement and destination replacement ordering remains unsupported
the broad Counter keyword action remains untrusted even though the two bounded capabilities are trusted
